clue.text: One multiply-spliced split may go wrong

indicators.note: letters that go wrong end up out of their proper order, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a split may go badly for someone who has been married several times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals that SPLIT MAY GO is rearranged. 'Spliced' is slang for married, so 'multiply-spliced' means married to several people.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spliced is slang for being married, and someone married many times over at once takes several wives or husbands.

clue.text: Skied at University College — beats reading!

indicators.note: in a down clue, something skied is sent upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
the LSE, London School of Economics, is a college of London University

explanation.surface: A student boasts that skiing at college beats studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skied' sends UP upward in this down light, giving PU. 'reading' is not studying: a pulse is a reading of heartbeats.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone's pulse means counting the heart's throbs per minute, a measured reading of them.

clue.text: Cavalryman entertaining a paid performer

indicators.note: the cavalryman holds the other letters inside, as a host entertains a guest

parts.note: a lancer is a mounted soldier armed with a lance
PD is the abbreviation for paid

explanation.surface: A cavalry soldier is entertained by a hired performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid' gives its standard abbreviation, and 'entertaining' has the cavalryman hold A and that abbreviation as guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer who performs on a club customer's lap is a kind of performer.

clue.text: Cast oblige — act all of that Irish play

indicators.note: the letters are cast about, thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to a cast to act every part of an Irish play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' signals rearranging OBLIGE ACT ALL OF; 'play' is a sport, not a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaelic game played with a round ball on a big pitch is a sport of Ireland, a play in the sense of a game.

clue.text: Girl that designed clothes, note

indicators.note: the word for designed wraps round the girl like clothing

parts.note: something designed for a purpose was meant for it
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A note about the girl who designed the clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here: MEANT clothes DI.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the third degree of a major or minor scale is a named note.

clue.text: Reserve carrot top as food for black guinea pig

parts.note: a sub, substitute, is a reserve player

indicators.note: the carrot's top goes inside the word for black, as food goes inside an eater

parts.note: jet is a deep black

indicators.note: takes the first letter of carrot

explanation.surface: A reserve feeds a carrot top to a black guinea pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guinea pig' looks like part of the pet scene but is the definition: someone experimented on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person used as a guinea pig is the subject of an experiment.

clue.text: Crack from pressure after endless questioning

indicators.note: the letter for pressure comes after the shortened word
the word for questioning loses its final letter, its end

parts.note: to quiz someone is to question them
P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Someone finally cracks under pressure after hours of relentless interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the Z from QUIZ, leaving QUI. 'Crack' is the definition in its sense of a witty remark, not a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a wisecrack, a short witty remark or joke.

clue.text: Reading, perhaps, about wedding?

parts.note: Reading is a university town, so its university is an example of a uni
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A town known for something to do with weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' is the English town with a university, not the act of reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a marriage, the joining of two people in matrimony.

clue.text: German player finally leading out youth section

definitions.text: German player finally leading out youth section

parts.words: German player finally leading out youth section
parts.note: the musician of the Hamelin legend who, when unpaid, played his pipe and led away the town's children

explanation.surface: A German musician at last leads off the youth section of an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'player' of Hamelin played a pipe and finally led out the town's children.
explanation.definitionFit: In the German legend the multicoloured piper of Hamelin led the town's children away.

clue.text: In which drivers see reflection of the moon?

definitions.text: In which drivers see reflection of the moon?

parts.words: In which drivers see reflection of the moon?
parts.note: to moon is to show one's backside, so a reflection of it is a view of behind, seen in a car's glass

explanation.surface: Where do motorists spot the moon reflected?
explanation.walkthrough: 'moon' means baring one's bottom; drivers see what is behind them reflected in this glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers check what is behind them in the glass mounted inside the windscreen.

clue.text: Consider moving trap to catch

parts.note: watch a speaker's moving mouth (trap is slang for mouth) to catch what is being said without hearing it

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about shifting a snare in order to catch an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is British slang for mouth; watching someone's mouth move lets a deaf person catch the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Following speech by studying the movement of a speaker's mouth is the skill described.

clue.text: Hairstyle with comb in it?

definitions.meaning: a tall rounded bouffant style of the 1960s
a bees' home holds honeycomb, not a hair comb

explanation.walkthrough: The 'comb' that suggests hairdressing is really honeycomb.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall domed hairdo is named after a hive's shape, and a hive literally contains honeycomb.

clue.text: Moving tree involves cutting a backward root out

indicators.note: the rearranged tree wraps round the reversed piece
the letters of tree are moved about into a new order
acid followed by a is read backwards

parts.note: a cutting remark is acid, sharp and biting

explanation.surface: Moving a tree means cutting back a root that grows the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' makes the anagram ERTE, which splits round the middle; 'backward' turns ACID plus A into ADICA. 'cutting' is the adjective (a cutting remark), not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To root out something is to destroy it completely, to wipe it out.

clue.text: Deliveryman's approach is to let bill accumulate

definitions.meaning: a bowler in cricket delivers the ball after a run towards the wicket
to ... a bill is to let a debt build

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball after running in to the wicket; the deliveryman is the bowler, not a courier.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler's approach to the crease is his run, and running up a debt means letting it mount.

clue.text: Declared withdrawal from FA Cup without a kick

parts.note: DEC is the cricket abbreviation for declared, ending an innings

indicators.note: FA is withdrawn, pulled back the other way

explanation.surface: A team pulls out of the FA Cup without kicking a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawal from' turns FA into AF. The FA Cup is England's football knockout competition, but 'Cup without a kick' is a cup of coffee with no caffeine.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee without caffeine gives no stimulant kick, so a cupful of it lacks that jolt.

clue.text: We pensioners should be attended to, without constant reality TV

indicators.note: the phrase is placed outside the letter for constant

parts.note: do, as in 'do us', means attend to or look after
us is the object form of we
OAPs are old-age pensioners
C is the constant for the speed of light

explanation.surface: Pensioners insist they should be looked after, without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the charade as the plea 'Do us OAPs!', i.e. look after us pensioners; 'without' means outside, so that plea surrounds the constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Documentary series following real people's lives are a form of reality television.

clue.text: Cheerful after salvaging job for the summer

indicators.note: the word for cheerful is placed after the salvaging word

parts.note: totting is British slang for scavenging useful items from rubbish tips
feeling up means feeling cheerful

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerful after landing a salvage job for the summer holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job for the summer' is not a holiday job: a summer is someone who sums, and adding figures up is his task.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as 'summer' meaning a person who does sums, the job is adding figures together.

clue.text: Blathering major turned navigator

indicators.note: the word for major is turned round

parts.note: big means major, large
Vitus Bering, the Danish navigator after whom the Bering Strait is named

explanation.surface: A rambling army major has turned to navigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes BIG into GIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Blathering and gibbering both mean talking nonsense rapidly.

clue.text: Drew truck round, as pedlar not peddling has

parts.note: a cart is a small truck for carrying goods
O is round in shape
the spelling pedlar contains a single D while peddling contains two

explanation.surface: A pedlar who has stopped selling drives his truck around.
explanation.walkthrough: The last phrase is about spelling: 'pedlar' has one D, unlike 'peddling'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have drawn a cartoon of someone is to have caricatured them in a drawing.

clue.text: Bring-a bottle party? Impossible. I'm afraid!

definitions.meaning: a party where you bring bottles has no cans
a casual refusal: sorry, I cannot

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a phrase: a party (do) with bottles, not cans.
explanation.definitionFit: The pidgin-style phrase for refusing is a casual way of saying something cannot be done.

clue.text: A measure of noise disturbed bed lice

indicators.note: the letters of bed lice are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Bed lice, once disturbed, make a measurable racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges BED LICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit for loudness measures sound intensity on a logarithmic scale.

clue.text: Opera composer's intrigue with leading lady

parts.note: a web of intrigue, a tangled plot
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the country's leading lady

explanation.surface: An opera composer becomes entangled in a plot with his prima donna.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' joining definition to wordplay. ER is the Queen's cipher (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Maria von Weber was the German who wrote Der Freischütz, an opera composer.

clue.text: Axe needed for brushwood

definitions.meaning: to axe a plan is to cancel it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' looks like a tool for clearing brushwood but is the verb meaning cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a project is to cancel it, and stunted bushes covering ground are also known by this word.

clue.text: Wig collector might set this game

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig
a collector sets things by, putting them aside

explanation.surface: A wig collector might stage this sporting game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' is slang for a toupee; collectors 'set by' or put by what they save.
explanation.definitionFit: The oval-ball sport named after an English school is a game.

clue.text: Swagger about officer commanding neat German guards

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding
neat is an old word for cattle, as is kine
the SS were Nazi Germany's guard units

explanation.surface: An officer's arrogant manner around the smart guards of a German unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is not tidy but the archaic word for cattle, so KINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Swagger is a cocky, arrogant self-confidence, the same as conceit shown off.

clue.text: Judge from Jerez I sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read upwards, backwards
the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A judge sent back something from Jerez, the Spanish sherry town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in jeREZ I Sent and read upward. Jerez is the Spanish town that gave sherry its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sizes things up assesses and judges them.

clue.text: African ace reaching new heights

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
the Golan Heights, a plateau between Israel and Syria

explanation.surface: An African sports star soars to fresh heights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heights' is the Golan Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Angola in south-west Africa is an African.

clue.text: Composer has all but cleared debt, it is reported

indicators.note: says the phrase is a spoken version of the answer

parts.note: someone who has nearly paid off a debt barely owes anything

explanation.surface: A composer has almost paid off what he owed, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it is reported' turns 'barely owes' into the sound of the French composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was the French composer of the Symphonie fantastique.

clue.text: Infernal runner got in way unknown number of times

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
in algebra y stands for an unknown number
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A runner kept getting in the way an unknown number of times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river: the one that flows round the Underworld of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the river of the Underworld runs through Hades, so it is an infernal runner.

clue.text: Standard message received on trip

indicators.note: in an across clue, the received message goes on after the trip

parts.note: a jolly is a pleasure outing, a jaunt
radio users say roger for message received

explanation.surface: A radio operator confirms receipt of a standard message while on an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a flag; the pirates' skull-and-crossbones.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the skull-and-crossbones pirate flag is a famous one.
